'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian occupation of Kharkiv Oblast]]
****[[Ukraine]] says that [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian forces]] are advancing on the city of [[Kharkiv]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-troops-advance-towards-kharkiv-ukraine-official-2022-06-19/ (Reuters)]
***[[Battle of Sievierodonetsk (2022)|Battle of Sievierodonetsk]]
****[[Russia]] says that its forces captured a district in the outskirts of [[Sieverodonetsk]] and that it launched [[Kalibr cruise missile]]s against a command centre in [[Dnipro]], killing several Ukrainian generals and officers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-it-struck-kharkiv-tank-repair-plant-with-iskander-missiles-2022-06-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Two people are killed when a car hits a [[roadside bomb]] in [[Kabul]]. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/blast-hits-car-in-afghan-capital--killing-two/47686404 (SwissInfo)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**A [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man is shot and killed by [[Israeli forces]] while attempting to cross the [[Israeli West Bank barrier|separation barrier]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-tel-aviv-israel-middle-east-west-bank-b72d92ca25870695ada2893152369dce (AP)]
*Militants attack two [[Church (building)|churches]], one of them [[Baptist]] and the other [[Catholic Church|Catholic]], in [[Kajuru]] [[Local government areas of Nigeria|LGA]] of [[Kaduna State]], [[Nigeria]]. Three members of the Catholic Church are killed and several more, mostly from the Baptist one, are [[Kidnapping in Nigeria|kidnapped]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-nigeria-west-africa-religion-93a0b12ecb42dfd2807ebd7046b62301 (AP)]  

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eighteen people are killed after a bus collided with a truck in [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://english.news.cn/africa/20220619/f78a86e4713f4312a9aaddbdf4cc3f42/c.html (Xinhua)]
*The [[Czech Republic]] records its highest temperature for the month of June, {{cvt|39.0|C|F}}, in [[Řež]]. Parts of [[Austria]], [[Germany]] and [[Poland]] also report record high temperatures. [https://denikn.cz/minuta/903473/ (Deník N)] [https://orf.at/stories/3271970/ (ORF)] [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/wetter-477.html (''Tagesschau'')] [https://www.axios.com/2022/06/19/heat-wave-europe-breaks-records (Axios)] [https://tvn24.pl/tvnmeteo/polska/polska-czerwcowy-rekord-temperatur-wyrownany-5756212 (TVN24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Lithuania–Russia relations]]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[Lithuania]] bans the transit of goods that are under EU sanctions through their territory to the Russian [[exclave]] of [[Kaliningrad Oblast|Kaliningrad]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/lithuania-says-sanctions-goods-kaliningrad-take-effect-saturday-2022-06-18/ (Reuters)]
*The [[European Union]] condemns the "structurally deficient" justice system in [[Bolivia]] and lack of "due process" in the trial of [[Jeanine Áñez]] and asks for her release. [https://amp.rpp.pe/mundo/latinoamerica/union-europea-senala-deficiencias-estructurales-en-juicio-contra-expresidenta-de-bolivia-jeanine-anez-noticia-1412665 (RPP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Colombian presidential election]]
**Citizens go to the polls to vote in the second round of the [[President of Colombia|Colombian president]]ial election. [https://www.eldiario.es/internacional/incertidumbre-marca-pulso-eleccion-historica-colombia_1_9094753.html (''elDiario.es'')]
**Left-wing candidate [[Gustavo Petro]] wins the presidential election with 50.44% of the vote, beating his opponent [[Rodolfo Hernández Suárez|Rodolfo Hernández]] who received 47.31% of the vote, according to preliminary results. [https://www.eldiario.es/internacional/izquierdista-gustavo-petro-gana-elecciones-presidenciales-colombia_1_9099056.html (''elDiario.es'')]
*[[2022 Nigerian elections]]
**[[2022 Nigerian gubernatorial elections]]
***[[2022 Ekiti State gubernatorial election]]
****Former state commissioner [[Abiodun Oyebanji]] of the [[All Progressives Congress]] defeats former Governor [[Olusegun Oni]] of the [[Social Democratic Party (Nigeria)|Social Democratic Party]] in the gubernatorial election. Oyebanji's win means that the APC has become the first party ever to win consecutive Ekiti gubernatorial elections. [https://dailytrust.com/breaking-inec-declares-apcs-oyebanji-winner-of-ekiti-governorship-election (''Daily Trust'')]
*[[Elections in Spain]]
**[[2022 Andalusian regional election]]
***Ruling [[People's Party of Andalusia]] wins a historic absolute majority, the first for a conservative party in [[Andalusia]]. [[Citizens (Spanish political party)|Citizens]], whose leader was the vice-president of the region, loses all the 21 deputies it had. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jun/19/spain-andalucia-vote-regional-election-peoples-party (''The Guardian'')] 
*[[2022 French legislative election]]
**French voters head to the polls to vote in the second round of the latest [[Legislative elections in France|legislative election]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2022/06/19/turnout-slightly-up-in-french-parliamentary-election-despite-heatwave (Euronews)]
**It is announced that [[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]]'s party [[La République En Marche!|Renaissance]] and its allies will not repeat an absolute majority in the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]]. [https://www.eldiario.es/internacional/macron-pierde-mayoria-absoluta-avance-alianza-izquierdas-melenchon_1_9098481.html (''elDiario.es'')]
*[[2022 Sri Lankan protests]], [[2022 Sri Lankan political crisis]]
**Four civilians and three soldiers were wounded in protest over gasoline shortage when the army opened fire for the first time to quell unrest, as [[Sri Lanka]] is suffering its worst [[2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis|economic crisis]] since independence. [https://news.am/eng/news/708002.html (''News.am'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Wimbledon Championships]]
**Russian tennis player [[Natela Dzalamidze]] changes her nationality to [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] and will participate in the upcoming [[The Championships, Wimbledon|Wimbledon]] tournament after Wimbledon [[Boycott of Russia and Belarus|banned]] [[Russia]]n and [[Belarus]]ian players from participating in the tournament. [https://www.eurosport.com/tennis/wimbledon/2022/russian-player-natela-dzalamidze-switches-nationality-to-georgian-in-order-to-compete-at-wimbledon-c_sto8999681/story.shtml (Eurosport)]
*[[FINA]], during its general congress, votes to disallow [[trans women]] [[Swimming (sport)|swimmers]] from [[Transgender people in sports|competing]] in high-level competitions. However, the body will convene a working group to develop a separate "open" category for them in select competitions. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/06/19/us/fina-vote-transgender-athletes/index.html (CNN)]
